title: Photo attributions
intro: Every photo used on the site, in Book 1, and in the Grammar handbook, listed for citation. Use this when you credit images for print, Scribus export, or YouTube. Lesson images come from each lesson file; grammar images come from each grammar chapter; homepage photos are added by hand.
citationNote: For Creative Commons works, credit the author, note the license, and link to the source page. For Pexels, credit the photographer and Pexels. Derivative treatments (polygon paint, background removal) still require attribution of the source photo.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 0 - Why this feels hard
entries.author: Michał Huniewicz
entries.notes: Kahva is the drink English would never change, and this map starts with why Bosnian will.

whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 0 - Why this feels hard
entries.author: Pudelek (Marcin Szala)
entries.notes: Kuća is one of the same few words this notebook will reuse while each system waits its turn.

entries.title: Old Bridge, Konjic
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 0 - Why this feels hard
entries.author: Julian Nyča
entries.notes: Most is a bridge on the map, and its pile day comes before any job chart.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee set, Baščaršija
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 1 - Why coffee is a she
entries.author: İhsan Işık
entries.notes: Kahva ends in a, so it belongs in the she pile, not because coffee is girly.

entries.title: Old Bridge, Konjic
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 1 - Why coffee is a she
entries.author: Julian Nyča
entries.notes: Most ends in t, so it belongs in the he pile.

entries.title: Zenit Beach, Neum
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 1 - Why coffee is a she
entries.author: Bdx
entries.notes: More ends in e, so it belongs in the leftover pile with pivo.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee set, Baščaršija
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 2 - Subject and the thing you want
entries.author: İhsan Işık
entries.notes: Ana wants the coffee as kahvu, and the ending moved for the want-it job on the same she-word.

entries.title: Počitelj panorama
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 2 - Subject and the thing you want
entries.author: Pudelek (Marcin Szala)
entries.notes: Kuća becomes kuću in the want-it job, the same she-pile move you saw on kahva.

entries.title: Sarajevsko bottle and glass
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 2 - Subject and the thing you want
entries.author: Fanny Schertzer
entries.notes: Pivo often stays pivo when you want the beer, the leftover stay-still habit beside the she-word move on kahva.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 3 - Of, from, none
entries.author: Michał Huniewicz
entries.notes: Nema kahve puts the of and none job on the coffee, so the ending is e, not the want-it u.

entries.title: Počitelj panorama
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 3 - Of, from, none
entries.author: Pudelek (Marcin Szala)
entries.notes: Kuće is the of form of the house, the same she-pile e you saw on kahve.

entries.title: Baščaršija, Sarajevo
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 3 - Of, from, none
entries.author: Kathleen Franklin
entries.notes: Iz Sarajeva uses the from job, so leftover Sarajevo becomes Sarajeva.

entries.title: Morića Han courtyard café, Sarajevo
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 4 - To, at, about
entries.author: JoJan
entries.notes: Dajem Ani kahvu marks Ana with the to form Ani while coffee stays in the want-it form as the gift.

entries.title: Apartment kitchen
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 4 - To, at, about
entries.author: Shixart1985
entries.notes: Ja sam u kući uses the at form, while Idem u kuću keeps into on the want-it ending.

entries.title: Outdoor café, Ferhadija, Sarajevo
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 4 - To, at, about
entries.author: Milan Suvajac
entries.notes: U Sarajevu is the at form Book 1 already used for being in the city.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee set, Baščaršija
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 5 - With, calling, the map
entries.author: İhsan Işık
entries.notes: S kahvom puts the with job on coffee, so the ending is om, not the want-it u.

entries.title: Friends toasting
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 5 - With, calling, the map
entries.author: Rennett Stowe from USA
entries.credit: Rennett Stowe from USA / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
entries.notes: Friends raise glasses with company, the same with job you hear in s Emirom and s Anom.

entries.title: Map of Bosnia and Herzegovina
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 5 - With, calling, the map
entries.author: NordNordWest
entries.notes: The preposition map only points. Each little word sends you back to a job you already own.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee set, Baščaršija
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 6 - Adjectives and possessives
entries.author: İhsan Işık
entries.notes: Moja kahva names the coffee with she-matching my, and moju kahvu wants that same drink.

entries.title: Počitelj panorama
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 6 - Adjectives and possessives
entries.author: Pudelek (Marcin Szala)
entries.notes: Moja kuća and moju kuću take the same she-matching ride you just saw on coffee.

entries.title: Old Bridge, Konjic
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 6 - Adjectives and possessives
entries.author: Julian Nyča
entries.notes: Moj most shows the he match, and that matching shape often stays still when you want the bridge.

entries.title: Morića Han courtyard café, Sarajevo
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 7 - Full pronouns vs short ones
entries.author: JoJan
entries.notes: Amira’s coffee at her place needs kod mene, the long form after the little word.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 7 - Full pronouns vs short ones
entries.author: Michał Huniewicz
entries.notes: Za mene keeps the long form because za sits in front of me.

entries.title: Friends toasting
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 7 - Full pronouns vs short ones
entries.author: Rennett Stowe from USA
entries.credit: Rennett Stowe from USA / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
entries.notes: Vidi me can use the short form because the doing-word carries the lean.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee set, Baščaršija
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 8 - Present tense for real
entries.author: İhsan Işık
entries.notes: Želim kahvu puts the I mark on the doing-word, which is the present map behind Ana’s Book 1 line.

entries.title: Morića Han courtyard café, Sarajevo
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 8 - Present tense for real
entries.author: JoJan
entries.notes: Pijem, radiš, and žele are the same who-row on different people at the same table.

entries.title: Mostar old town
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 8 - Present tense for real
entries.author: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
entries.credit: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
entries.notes: Idem is the present of ići, a pest that refuses a fake ićim when someone is going now.

entries.title: Burek
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 9 - Eat versus eat up
entries.author: photo Moma SM
entries.credit: photo Moma SM / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
entries.notes: Jedem burek is the open bite, and pojesti is eat the burek up when the tray is the finish line.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 9 - Eat versus eat up
entries.author: Michał Huniewicz
entries.notes: Pijem kahvu keeps the cup open, while popiti seals the same drink as drink up.

entries.title: Old Bridge, Konjic
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 9 - Eat versus eat up
entries.author: Julian Nyča
entries.notes: Idem na most keeps going open, and otići seals leaving as the whole trip.

entries.title: Mostar old town
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 10 - Past
entries.author: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
entries.credit: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
entries.notes: A stroll through town is still Bio sam for Emir and Bila sam for Ana, because the past piece follows who walked.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee set, Baščaršija
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 10 - Past
entries.author: İhsan Işık
entries.notes: Pio sam kahvu and Pila sam kahvu split on who drank, not on coffee switching piles.

entries.title: Počitelj panorama
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 10 - Past
entries.author: Pudelek (Marcin Szala)
entries.notes: Išla sam kući keeps -la on Ana, while the house stays the same she-word from earlier chapters.

entries.title: Ferhadija, Sarajevo
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 11 - Future, want, must, do it
entries.author: Mark Chorlton from Stockport, UK
entries.credit: Mark Chorlton from Stockport, UK / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
entries.notes: Idite na most is the polite command shape, while Idi stays blunt for one friend.

entries.title: Bosanska Kahva
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 11 - Future, want, must, do it
entries.author: Brenda Annerl
entries.notes: Ja ću piti kahvu hangs the future on ću in second place plus the infinitive, not on an English will stuck in front of pijem.

entries.title: Friends toasting
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 11 - Future, want, must, do it
entries.author: Rennett Stowe from USA
entries.credit: Rennett Stowe from USA / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
entries.notes: Hoću, moram, trebam, and mogu are the short café row for want, must, need, and can.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee set, Baščaršija
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 13 - Patterns English speakers get wrong
entries.author: İhsan Işık
entries.notes: Želim kahvu still carries the she pile and the want-it job on the same coffee from Chapter 1 and Chapter 2.

entries.title: Old Bridge, Konjic
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 13 - Patterns English speakers get wrong
entries.author: Julian Nyča
entries.notes: Most stays in the he pile, and Želim most often keeps the list form in the want-it job.

entries.title: Počitelj panorama
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 13 - Patterns English speakers get wrong
entries.author: Pudelek (Marcin Szala)
entries.notes: Kuća becomes kuću in the want-it job, the same she-pile move the review keeps asking you to name.

entries.title: Morića Han courtyard café, Sarajevo
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 12 - Clitics and second place
entries.author: JoJan
entries.notes: Ana says Ja se zovem Ana at the café, and se sits in second place after Ja.

entries.title: Bosnian coffee set, Baščaršija
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 12 - Clitics and second place
entries.author: İhsan Işık
entries.notes: Daj mi kahvu parks mi in second place after Daj, while kahvu keeps the want-it job on coffee.

entries.title: Friends toasting
whereUsed: Grammar · Chapter 12 - Clitics and second place
entries.author: Rennett Stowe from USA
entries.credit: Rennett Stowe from USA / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
entries.notes: Pio sam pivo puts Pio first and parks the little past helper sam in second place.
